title: Superhuman Pricing: Plans, Costs and Value (2026)
summary: Superhuman pricing is higher than most email tools, and this cost-per-message table provides the information missing from their official pricing page.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


After those comparisons, a few practical questions remain, and none of them changes which plan you should pick.


Does Superhuman have a free plan? Not as a permanent tier we can confirm, which is the main reason it sits apart from rivals that offer one.


Check Superhuman's own pricing page before you assume otherwise. If a trial is offered, use it to measure your real daily volume instead of guessing.


Can I cancel Superhuman and get a refund? You can cancel, but we haven't verified the refund terms, so don't assume a pro-rated return.


Cancel before the renewal date, keep the confirmation, and ask support in writing whether the unused portion is refundable. That matters most on an annual plan, where a mistimed renewal costs the most.


Does Superhuman work with Outlook and Gmail accounts? Yes, it connects to both Gmail and Outlook accounts, and it sits on top of your existing mailbox instead of replacing it.


That means leaving costs you the interface, not your mail. Confirm that your particular setup, such as a company-managed Microsoft account, is allowed by your IT administrator before you pay.


### Is the annual plan cheaper than paying monthly?


You will normally find annual billing discounted against monthly, but we won't quote a figure we haven't confirmed. Do the arithmetic yourself: divide the annual price by twelve and set it against the monthly price.


Then ask whether you'll still be using the client in month four. A discount only helps if you stay long enough to collect it, and it makes a mid-year exit more expensive.


Do students or nonprofits get a Superhuman discount? We couldn't confirm a student or nonprofit programme.


Ask Superhuman's support directly and get any discount in writing before paying. If none exists, the cheaper client or the rival's free tier from earlier in the article is the better route for anyone whose email volume doesn't justify the full price.
